reports.title: The Local Government Act, 2022
reports.description: Sierra Leone's current local-government law, verified directly via download (hosted on the Ministry of Finance's own site). Its own preamble states the Act's purpose is "to repeal and replace the Local Government Act 2004." Section 49: "A local council shall be financed from (a) its own revenue collections; (b) central government grants for devolved functions; and (c) transfers of services delegated from Government Ministries." Section 49(4) lists own-source revenue categories including "grants (recurrent and capital) for devolved functions from the Government; development grants; grants for devolved services from the MDAs; precepts from local taxes; property tax; licences; fees and charges; share of mining revenues; interests and dividends." Section 50: "Each year a local council shall be paid tied grants (a) for the discharge of the devolved functions; (b) for the development of its locality; (c) towards its administrative cost." Section 53: "Parliament shall appropriate to a Local Council as a tied grant for each devolved service at least the amount necessary to continue the operation and maintenance of that service" — a statutory grant-adequacy floor, comparable in function (though not identical in mechanism) to the FNACT/30%-floor provisions found elsewhere in this branch (e.g. Mali's superseded 2017 code).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, currently in force.

reports.title: The Sierra Leone Gazette (Extraordinary) — Grant Distribution to Local Councils, FY2022
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Sierra Leone
reports.region: Freetown, Makeni, Koidu New Sembehun, Kenema and Bo City Councils, plus other named local councils, Sierra Leone
reports.description: An official Gazette publication naming individual local councils ("Freetown City Council, Makeni City Council, Koidu New Sembehun City Council, Kenema City Council, Bo City Council" grouped as Category A with a needs-adjustment factor of 1.5 for primary health services) and setting out detailed weighted-distribution formulas: primary health services allocated via "Lump sum-45%" plus "Needs adjusted population-55%" (with three population need-adjustment categories, factors 1.5/2.0/3.0); education via "Lump sum weighted 40%", "Total Enrolment-35%", and "Population of School Going age (2-14 years)-25%"; secondary health via bed-occupancy (15%), population (25%), under-five consultations (10%), and hospital utilisation rate (20%). Real aggregate totals stated: total allocation to local councils (direct + indirect) Le 150,845,185,600; Health Care Services sector Le 42,185,900,000; Education sector Le 37,058,685,600 (direct Le 11,900,000,000 plus indirect Le 25,158,685,600). Per-council allocation figures appear in detailed tables later in the document that were not independently re-extracted this session (noted as a specific follow-up lead).
reports.cadence_note: One-off annual Gazette publication; this is the FY2022 edition.

reports.title: Auditor-General's Annual Report 2024
reports.region: Bonthe District Council and Karene District Council, Sierra Leone (among other audited entities nationally)
reports.description: ASSL's own annual audit report, independently re-verified this session (hosted on the Audit Service's own site). Names Bonthe District Council with a qualitative finding: "Bonthe District Council however, received a modified opinion due to issues such as improper recording of own-source revenue, payments lacking sufficient documentation, and misclassified expenditures in the PETRA accounting system." Names Karene District Council with a finding on grant-disbursement timing: "In Karene, for example, rollover allocations for all sectors were received on 23rd February 2025, while only one quarter was released on 8th August 2024, eight months after the start of the year" — documenting a real, named-council instance of the pattern (late/irregular central-government fiscal transfers) found repeatedly across this branch's Auditor-General-sourced findings in other countries. NOTE: this report contains no quantitative revenue/expenditure/transfer AMOUNTS for either council in the passages located this session — narrower in evidentiary strength than the Auditor-General reports minted for Malawi/Zambia/Zimbabwe/Chad earlier in this same population-priority push, which did name specific figures.
